title: Known unenforced pipeline artifact constraints (validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs gaps)
content:
Recorded from #34's review (merged PR #51, 2026-08-20) so a future 'add a constraint to a schema' task does not re-discover this expensively; corrected and extended at #61 (merged to main as cc41c11, 2026-08-22) and again at #40 (merged to main as 7a052d3, 2026-08-22). plugins/pipeline/schemas/status.schema.json has NO entry in validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's AGENT_RULES table, so status.json is never validated against it at all, by anything. Separately, and more generally, that walker's own header states maxLength is unimplemented (the token 'maxLength' appears exactly once in validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, in the comment that says so) -- so even a schema that IS registered in AGENT_RULES would not have a maxLength constraint enforced by the generic walker; a schema author needs either a bespoke check (the established precedent is the groundOpenQuestions check in validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, re-derive with `git grep -n 'function groundOpenQuestions' plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs`) or a dedicated corpus-conformance test suite (the pattern #34 used for status.schema.json's verdict-field caps: see knowledge/living-context/testing--status-schema-verdict-cap-enforcement.json). Practical consequence: a maxLength or pattern constraint added to any schema file in this repo is documentation, not a guard, until one of those two enforcement paths exists for it. #34 explicitly declined to close this gap generally (out_of_scope: 'Adding maxLength or pattern support to validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's schema walker... would change the validation behaviour of EVERY schema at once' and 'Registering status.json in AGENT_RULES... is a new enforcement surface with its own fail-open/fail-closed design questions, not a schema annotation'). If the owner wants either closed, it is scoped as its own issue, not a schema-annotation follow-on.

CORRECTION FILED AT #40, HIGH SEVERITY, RAISED INDEPENDENTLY BY TWO REVIEWERS (spec.json's own knowledge-drift claim and review.json's DBA round-2 finding), SUPERSEDES THE ENFORCEMENT BOUNDARY THIS FILE PREVIOUSLY DREW. The boundary this file recorded through #61 -- 'does the walker implement the keyword, with status.schema.json called out as the one schema absent from AGENT_RULES' -- implied that a walker-implemented constraint on an AGENT_RULES-REGISTERED schema IS a guard. WALKER SUPPORT IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. The DOMINANT boundary, and the one that screens off every other fail-open degradation before it is even reached, is whether the STOPPING AGENT'S `agent_type` MATCHES an `AGENT_RULES` key. `AGENT_RULES` (`validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:93`) is keyed by BARE role names ('secops', not 'pipeline:secops'); `checkArtifacts` does `AGENT_RULES[String(agentType || '').toLowerCase()]` and `if (!rules) return { failures }` (re-derive: `git grep -n 'export function checkArtifacts' -A3 plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs`), so a plugin-NAMESPACED agent type ('pipeline:secops') MISSES the lookup and returns ZERO failures for every agent, every artifact and every rule -- before any root, mtime or active-issue resolution runs, and before the walker gets anywhere near a keyword it does or does not implement. THIS MAKES THE VALIDATOR INERT IN EVERY PLUGIN-INSTALLED PROJECT, which is the shipping product's DEFAULT deployment. Measured with the shipped hook on a 7-violation fixture, four cells: 'secops' -> block naming all seven; 'SecOps' -> block; 'pipeline:secops' -> SILENT; 'agent-pipeline:secops' -> SILENT. Corroborated by an emission census over one machine's ~/.claude/projects transcripts (window 2026-08-21; population 1680 files / 366,314 lines across 13 repositories that carry any transcript, of which the 8-repo union of block-bearing and namespaced-dispatch-bearing repos holds 1662 files / 362,734 lines -- state the window and the grain with any of these figures, they are a live corpus that only grows): 56 genuine blocks, every one in a project dispatching BARE agent names because the plugin is disabled there and its agents are local `.claude/agents/*.md` files; ZERO across 670 plugin-namespaced dispatches in SEVEN repositories (645 excluding the measuring session's own 25), including an adopting project (nsmedia-platform) with 362 of them at the project-directory grain the measuring recipe actually groups by (365 only at the coarser REPOSITORY grain, which sums a second, different project directory for the same repo carrying 3 unrelated feature-dev:code-reviewer dispatches -- name the grain in the same sentence as the figure, per the rule that a number carries its window and its grain). FILED AS #66 (2026-08-21). The four OTHER fail-open degradations this file already named (node absent, plugin root unset, active issue unresolvable, artifact mtime over 30 minutes) are all still real but are SCREENED OFF by this one for a namespaced agent type: none of them is ever reached, because the AGENT_RULES lookup miss returns first. A schema author's correct mental model is therefore: a walker-implemented constraint on an AGENT_RULES-registered schema is a guard ONLY where the pipeline dispatches bare agent names (a repo running local, non-namespaced `.claude/agents/*.md`); it is DOCUMENTATION everywhere the plugin is installed and dispatches under its own namespace, independent of whether the constraint itself is implemented by the walker. THE RECORD HAS AN EXPIRY, stated so a future reader does not trust it past its shelf life: the correct outcome for #66 is that somebody fixes the AGENT_RULES lookup, on which day this correction becomes false with no event that notices it (a silence has no event) -- re-derive the four-cell fixture rather than trust this paragraph once #66 is closed.

TWO NARROWER GAPS FILED AT #40, MEDIUM SEVERITY, COST REAL IMPLEMENTATION TIME THIS RUN AND WILL COST IT AGAIN. (i) `node plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs <file>` as a standalone CLI invocation VALIDATES NOTHING: it exits 0 on deliberate garbage and on a nonexistent path. Only `--self-test` and the hook's stdin path (the SubagentStop path the correction above concerns) do real validation work; the orchestrator used the bare-file form repeatedly on #40 and read `rc=0` as confirmation before controlling for it. (ii) `checkArtifacts`'s `rootsOverride` parameter takes REPO ROOTS, not `.pipeline` directories: `pipelineDirs` joins `.pipeline` onto each element of `rootsOverride`, so passing a `.pipeline` directory itself yields zero dirs walked and a VACUOUS clean pass with no error raised. Both (i) and (ii) are the same trap class as the `validate()` root-argument trap two paragraphs below: a caller passing the wrong shape gets a clean bill of health that is output-indistinguishable from a genuinely clean tree.

CORRECTION FILED AT #61, RETRACTED AND REPLACED after a second look -- recorded so the retracted claim is not re-discovered nor re-asserted. An earlier version of this entry claimed peer-review.schema.json's 7 $ref-declared sub-schemas (the ba/dba/devops/secops/dev/qa/design_review role blocks, each {"$ref": "#/definitions/panelVerdict"}) were undereferenced by validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, leaving a Phase 4 panel's per-role verdicts (including a SecOps VETO) unvalidated. THAT CLAIM WAS WRONG, and its own author found the reason: the wrongness was in the caller of validate(), not in validate() itself. `export function validate(value, schema, root, pathStr = "", errors = [])` (re-derive with `git grep -n 'export function validate' plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs`) takes the ROOT SCHEMA OBJECT as its third parameter -- the object `deref()` walks a `$ref` pointer against -- and the original measurement passed the STRING "peer-review" there, mistaking it for a label. `deref(schema, root)` then indexed a string with `schemaAt`, which returns `undefined` for every `$ref`, so every $ref-typed property silently validated as absent and every call returned `[]` (a clean bill) regardless of the document's actual shape. Reproduced, same document, only the third argument changed: `root = "peer-review"` (string) gives `qa.verdict="LGTM" -> []` and `qa=12345 -> []`; `root = <the loaded schema object>` gives `qa.verdict="LGTM" -> ["/qa/verdict: \"LGTM\" is not one of [...]"]`, `qa.verdict=42 -> ["/qa/verdict: expected type \"string\", got number"]`, and `qa=12345 -> ["/qa: expected type \"object\", got number"]`. So THE DURABLE FINDING IS A CALLER-SIDE TRAP, not a validator defect: pass anything other than the root schema object as validate()'s third argument and every $ref-declared constraint anywhere under it silently stops being checked, while the call still returns a clean `[]` -- a caller cannot tell that apart from a genuinely valid document. This repo's $ref use is concentrated in peer-review.schema.json (7 of them, all the role blocks), so the constraint an author is likeliest to lose this way is exactly the panel-verdict enum, including a SecOps VETO's shape. In actual production use this trap is not live: AGENT_RULES never calls validate() with a bad root (checkArtifacts always passes the loaded schema object it just parsed), and the panel-verdict shape IS validated -- confirmed end to end against the real CLI with a scratch .pipeline dir and a copied schemas dir, all four crafted defects (qa.verdict="LGTM", qa=12345 whole-block-replaced, qa.verdict=42 wrong-type, qa missing required verdict) correctly blocked. The trap is a hazard for a FUTURE ad-hoc caller of validate() (a new script, a REPL check, a debugging one-off), not a gap in the shipped path. 

TWO REAL RESIDUALS CARRIED FORWARD FROM #61's Phase 4 panel (SecOps/QA lens, gate-phase-entry.mjs -- filed here as the nearest 'known gaps in the validation/guard tooling' home, not validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs itself; deferred rather than fixed because folding either into #61's diff would have widened a halting-control change past its own tripwire). Both verified true by direct code reading at origin/main cc41c11. (a) FAIL-OPEN CATCH DISCARDS ALREADY-COMPUTED DECISIONS: `main()`'s only try/catch is the outer one at the module's self-run entry point (re-derive: `git grep -n 'try {' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs | tail -5`, paired with `git grep -n 'function main' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`), and it wraps the WHOLE call to `main()`, including the `for (const dir of candidateDirs(pipelineDir))` loop that accumulates `results.push(decideForDir(dir, now))`. If `decideForDir` throws on any ONE dir, the exception unwinds through that loop and the catch reports fail-open silence -- discarding every decision already computed for every OTHER dir in the same sweep, including a genuine `refused` (rc 2) result. A real refusal for issue A can vanish because issue B's record made a later iteration throw. (b) `eventsSatisfy` CAN THROW ON THE ARTIFACT-ABSENT PATH: `function eventsSatisfy(events, tokens) { if (!Array.isArray(events) || tokens.length === 0) return false; ... }` checks `Array.isArray(events)` but never checks that `tokens` is itself an array (or even defined) before reading `tokens.length`. `checkOne`'s fallback (`return { ok: eventsSatisfy(events, subRow.tokens), artifact: "absent" }`, reached when the artifact file does not exist) passes `subRow.tokens` straight through, so a `PREREQUISITES` row (or `also` sub-row) that carries a `file` but no `tokens` key throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` the moment its file is absent. NOT REACHABLE TODAY: every row in the shipped `PREREQUISITES` table (re-derive by reading the literal, or `git grep -n '^const PREREQUISITES' plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`) carries a `tokens` key, including the `also` sub-row #61 added, so this is latent, not live. It becomes live the moment a future row is authored without one -- and per (a), if it throws, it also erases every OTHER issue dir's already-computed decision in the same sweep, so the two residuals compound. Both are written up in full in the ledger comments on issue #61 (two comments on the closed issue carry the fix-round detail); not filed as a fresh issue by #61 itself, per the net-issues-down constraint, but flagged here so a future author touching either function sees the coupling before adding a tokens-less row.

CORRECTION FILED AT #63 (merged to main as 012db65, PR #77), LOW SEVERITY: this entry's own inventory of unimplemented keywords was itself stale and needed the same discipline #63 applied to the guard's comments -- assert what is verifiable, not a paraphrase that decays. The walker's header (`validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:29-30`) names SIX keywords it does not implement, not the two ('maxLength or pattern') this entry previously singled out: `if/then, format, pattern, maxLength, oneOf/anyOf` (re-derive: `sed -n '29,30p' plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs`). Of those six, `if`/`then` is the only one with a LIVE INERT constraint behind it in a shipped schema today, so it is the one most likely to mislead a reader of this entry's prior wording into thinking only length/pattern-style keywords are at risk. `plugins/pipeline/schemas/impl-report.schema.json` declares (re-derive: `grep -n '\"if\"\|\"then\"\|justification' plugins/pipeline/schemas/impl-report.schema.json`) an `if` (`status` is `PARTIAL` or `SKIP`) / `then` (`requirement_index`, `requirement_text`, `status`, `notes`, `justification` all required) rule on each `requirement_check` entry -- i.e. a PARTIAL or SKIP requirement check is supposed to be REQUIRED to carry a `justification`. Because the walker never evaluates `if`/`then` at all (confirmed by the same header line, and by `validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs` containing no `if`/`then`-keyword handling in its walker function), that requirement is enforced by NOBODY: a PARTIAL or SKIP requirement_check with no justification passes `checkArtifacts` clean today, exactly like the AGENT_RULES-lookup-miss and maxLength gaps already recorded above. Same practical consequence as the rest of this entry: this is documentation, not a guard, until a bespoke check (the `groundOpenQuestions` precedent) or a corpus-conformance test closes it. Recorded so a future reader does not read the prior 'maxLength and pattern' framing and conclude `if`/`then` is safe.

CORRECTED AT #106's ARCHIVAL PASS (2026-09-02), PER THIS ENTRY'S OWN STATED EXPIRY CONDITION -- 'the correct outcome for #66 is that somebody fixes the AGENT_RULES lookup, on which day this correction becomes false with no event that notices it'. That day is now. #66 CLOSED, fixed inside #106's own commit series (present on main since fc9a171, 'feat: add the run-ownership seam and its leaf predicate module (#106)'): `checkArtifacts` (validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs, re-derive the current line with `git grep -n 'export function checkArtifacts' plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs`, currently :1031) now computes `const agent = bareRole(agentType);` BEFORE the `AGENT_RULES[agent]` lookup (re-derive `bareRole`'s own line with `git grep -n 'export function bareRole'`, currently still :493 in this file), so a plugin-namespaced dispatch (`pipeline:secops`) and a bare one (`secops`) now resolve identically. The bare `validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:93` citation this entry previously carried does not resolve from the repository root either (the file has grown since #40/#61/#63); `AGENT_RULES`'s own declaration is now at :100 (`git grep -n '^const AGENT_RULES'`) -- cite the grep, not the line number, since this file has already drifted three times.

RE-VERIFIED DIRECTLY IN THIS PASS, not copied from #106's own claim: `checkArtifacts('secops', {}, Date.now(), [root])`, `checkArtifacts('SecOps', ...)`, `checkArtifacts('pipeline:secops', ...)` and `checkArtifacts('agent-pipeline:secops', ...)` against the same fixture root all now return `verdict: 'checked'`, not one of them 'no-rules'/silent -- the four-cell split this entry recorded ('secops'/'SecOps' block, 'pipeline:secops'/'agent-pipeline:secops' silent) NO LONGER HOLDS. THE SENTENCE 'THIS MAKES THE VALIDATOR INERT IN EVERY PLUGIN-INSTALLED PROJECT' IS NOW FALSE AND MUST NOT BE READ AS A CURRENT CLAIM; it remains correct only as a description of the tree between #40 (7a052d3) and #106 (fc9a171).

#128 (merged 2e28f8d, 'A fail-open validator path must announce that it failed open (#66 property 2, #115)') closed a SEPARATE, adjacent silence this entry did not previously name: even with the lookup fixed, `checkArtifacts` returning zero failures was output-identical whether it had checked a clean tree or never matched an agent at all (both were 0 bytes of stdout, exit 0). `checkArtifacts` now returns a `verdict` field alongside `failures` (`checked` / `no-rules` / `no-pipeline-root` / `no-active-issue` / `unnamed-run` / `unnamed-run-ambiguous`), and a new `announceLine(result)` function (validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:1222) writes one attribution line to STDERR -- `agent-pipeline SubagentStop: agent=<x> verdict=<y> [issue=<n>] violations=<n>[; detail]` -- for any session that resolved at least one candidate root (`result.roots` truthy); a genuinely non-pipeline session with no `.pipeline` directory anywhere still emits nothing, which is the one silence #128 states it deliberately leaves. `hooks/subagent-stop.sh` (:40) was itself changed in the same commit to STOP DISCARDING STDERR (the invocation dropped its `2>/dev/null`), which is what actually carries `announceLine`'s output to a reader; stdout is untouched and still carries only the decision JSON (or nothing). #128 also closed #115 in the same commit (a run directory BA could name in none of ISSUE_DIR_RE's sanctioned forms previously opted out of validation silently; `checkArtifacts` now validates such a run when it is the unique candidate via a new `unnamedRunDirs()` path), not otherwise this entry's subject.

THE LIVE RESIDUAL, RESTATED PER THE OWNER'S RE-SCOPING OF #66 (reopened 2026-09-02): #128's fix proves the validator classifies the agent set correctly IN THE SOURCE TREE (derived from `agents/*.md` frontmatter -- configuration, not history, per the rule that inferring an expectation from what ran rather than what should run makes an incomplete check look complete). It cannot observe whether a DEPLOYED PLUGIN CACHE in an adopting project has ever fired at all: an installed copy that has never matched any agent and a freshly-updated one that has never had an opportunity to run are still indistinguishable from OUTSIDE that project's own transcripts, because `announceLine` only ever writes to that project's own stderr, and nothing sweeps the fleet of adopting projects to confirm any given one is running current-enough code to benefit from this fix at all. That is the honest current scope of #66 as reopened; do not read this paragraph past whatever event closes #66 next.
